title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer + Helm & Terraform modules
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: when deploying Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) at scale we need a repeatable, least-privilege RBAC bootstrap flow that works across the private-installer, Helm charts, and Terraform modules. This PR introduces automation for tenant-level RBAC bootstrapping so operator scripts and the private-installer can create the minimal set of roles, rolebindings, and service accounts required for tenant isolation and operator workflows without manual steps.

Summary of changes: added a set of opinionated, parameterized RBAC manifests and Terraform/Helm helpers; created automation entrypoints used by the private-installer; added validation e2e smoke checks and CI jobs to prevent drift. The description below lists the important artifacts and rationale.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces rbac/templates/tenant-bootstrap.yaml - parameterized Kubernetes Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding, ServiceAccount templates for tenant bootstrap.
- Adds helm/chart-templates/rbac.yaml and values schema to support tenant-scoped bootstraps via helm install/upgrade.
- Adds terraform/modules/rbac-bootstrap/ that wraps k8s provider resources + outputs for integration with private-installer provisioning steps.
- Adds private-installer/hooks/bootstrap_rbac.sh which calls terraform/helm entrypoints in a safe, idempotent fashion with retry/backoff.
- Adds an automation e2e smoke test (tests/rbac_bootstrap_smoke.py) to validate expected permissions for tenant-admin and operator service accounts.
- Adds CI linting & policy checks (conftest/gatekeeper rules) to ensure manifests follow least-privilege constraints.

Backward compatibility & upgrade notes: this change is additive. Existing clusters will not be modified unless operators opt-in to run the new bootstrap automation. The helm changes are guarded behind a new values flag (rbac.bootstrap.enabled=false by default) to avoid accidental role deployments. Terraform module versioning is bumped and documented in the module README.

Testing and rollout: ran local private-installer end-to-end with a three-node k8s cluster (kind) and a mocked KMS. CI includes a smoke job that deploys the helm chart with bootstrap enabled into a disposable cluster and ensures the tenant SA can list/watch expected resources. Local perf: bootstrap script completes ~18s on average in CI envs.

Security considerations: roles are intentionally scoped to `namespaces/tenant-{id}` and use explicit rule lists. We forbid granting cluster-admin. Gatekeeper policies are included to prevent wildcard verbs on sensitive resources.

Checklist:
- [x] rbac templates and helm values schema added
- [x] terraform module and README added
- [x] private-installer integration script added
- [x] smoke tests + CI job added
- [x] documentation snippets for upgrade path added to docs/private/rbac.md

Related: ENG-4521 (tenant isolation automation), DEVOPS-1120 (private-installer onboarding).

release_notes: Adds automated tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private deployments. Exposes helm flag rbac.bootstrap.enabled (default false). Adds terraform rbac-bootstrap module and private-installer automation entrypoint. New smoke test validates least-privilege assignments.
notes_for_ops: Operators: opt-in by setting helm value `rbac.bootstrap.enabled=true` or invoking terraform module per-module README. The installer script `bootstrap_rbac.sh` will perform idempotent creates and will not modify existing roles unless --force is supplied.
